## Five training zones from these two thresholds

| Domain |  |  | Intensity (W) | Heart rate (bpm) | RPE | Lactate (mmol/L) |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| Moderate | Zone 1 | below LT1 | \< 62 | \< 124 | \< 8 | \< 1.1 |
|  | Zone 2 |  | 62–83 | 124–140 | 8–9 | 1.1–1.4 |
| Heavy | Zone 3 | LT1 to LT2 | 83–149 | 140–182 | 9–14 | 1.4–4.2 |
| Severe | Zone 4 | above LT2 | 149–170 | 182–191 | 14–16 | 4.2–6.1 |
|  | Zone 5 |  | \> 170 | \> 191 | \> 16 | \> 6.1 |

## Predicted performance

What the threshold predicts for a race, from the equations of Heuberger
et al. 2018 (refitted).

| Race | From the threshold | Expected average power | 95 of 100 athletes |
|----|----|----|----|
| 45-min time trial | LT2, Log-Poly-ModD_(max) at 149 W | 172 W † | 138 to 206 W |
| † The threshold lies outside the range of the athletes the equation was built on: an extrapolation, to read with care. |  |  |  |

How to read it: athletes with an LT2 like this one averaged 172 W in a
45-min time trial; 95 of 100 of them averaged between 138 and 206 W.

## What to double-check

9 of 10 checks of the data passed.
